hypothesis: A repository-committed checksum-pinned BuildOpt Wrapper backed by an optional centralized Gradle HTTP cache and a separate typed decision store can learn from ordinary builds, activate only verified profitable actions, and produce positive cumulative wall-time value against optimized native Gradle with negligible native-retention overhead.

scorecard.requirement: four generated committed files, one private token source and one repeated wrapper command; no global BuildOpt install or hand-authored profile
all tested distributions are immutable, checksum verified and atomically installed; tamper, non-HTTPS or excessive redirect, and traversal reject
arguments, environment boundary, streams, process tree, signals and exit status match direct Wrapper behavior on Linux, macOS and Windows
all comparable outputs satisfy their frozen equivalence contract and product-attributable failures equal zero
cache objects never authorize decisions and state objects never become Gradle cache hits
local no-op decision path is at most 100 ms p50 and 250 ms p95; unavailable-service fallback is at most 500 ms p95
additional trial compute is at most 5 percent of natural runner-minutes with one concurrent trial per repository
no repository-name, task-name, path-extension or manually authored evaluated-profile rules
at least three of five public repository families activate or install an independently qualified action
at least three of five families have a positive paired or block-bootstrap 95 percent lower bound
complete signed cumulative net value is positive after all BuildOpt costs
at least three families repay learning and publication within 30 compatible requested builds
at least one generic reviewed transformation remains net positive over at least 15 later compatible commits without BuildOpt runtime action dependency
every credited runtime profile has measured active saving and a native counterfactual; inactive actions receive zero saving
every invocation exposes a recomputable decision, binding generation, action, fallback reason and gross, cost and net values without secrets
